mira: Quick question — need guidance. My team wants me onsite at a client in Lisbon for 30 days (company-funded travel). Do I need to change homebase? Will WFH stipend / laptop shipping / payroll tax be affected? Who do I talk to about housing stipend vs WFH allowance? @sarah (People Ops) @jamal (Payroll) cc: @ana
sarah (People Ops): Congrats! Short answers: short-term secondments <90 days usually don't force a homebase change, but local payroll/tax rules matter. We need exact dates, country, and confirmation you'll stay on Redwood payroll.
mira: Dates: 2026-04-15 -> 2026-05-15. We'll stay on Redwood payroll. Company may book an apartment. Also: do I still get monthly WFH $150 or is it paused/prorated? If company books housing, is that taxable?
jamal (Payroll): If you remain on Redwood payroll and are in PT for 30 days, Portugal's 183-day tax residence rule won't be triggered. Payroll-level issues: social security and withholding depend on bilateral agreements. Company-paid housing can be a taxable fringe both in US and PT. We'll need to consult local tax counsel for final treatment. For the WFH stipend: we prorate based on days you are actually working remote. Please submit the temporary location declaration (Workday).
sarah (People Ops): Re: stipend policy — WFH allowance is for your primary remote/home workspace. For months where you're onsite >50% of business days, People Ops pauses that month's stipend and prorates. Fill the "Temporary Location" form (Workday link) and tag People Ops. We'll route to Payroll and Finance for tax coding.
mira: Filing the form now. Who handles apartment booking? Can People Ops book it and code as travel (not relocation)? Also visa — do I need a short-stay work visa to "work" from client office for 30 days?
